content:
incident-bot: Paging: elevated tail latency observed on /v1/chat/generate (pool: europe-west-2). Alert: batch queue depth > 90th pct, continuous batching fallback triggered. Auto-suppressing low-priority jobs.

jamal: I’m on it. seeing CPU on g4-pool-2 saturated, nvlink queues spiking. Latency jump ~+500-800ms P95 -> P99.

maria: @jamal do you want me to start traffic shaping now or hand off to infra?

jamal: Start live mitigation: reduce continuous_batch_window_ms to 8ms (was 22ms) for pool-2, and set max_batch_tokens=1024 -> 512 for chat-heavy model variants. That should push latency down but will drop throughput.

kevin: Command ready. Running patch:
```
rictl patch pool pool-2 --set continuous_batch_window_ms=8 --set max_batch_tokens=512 --reason="emergency oncall throttle"
```

sophie: Applying now. Will also enable fast-fail for tiny-priority requests (ttl priority=low) to avoid tail spikes.

incident-bot: Action logged: patch by sophie at 3600000520.

jamal: Also temp quota caps for anonymous and trial keys: set rate limit to 10 req/s per key for 30m.

maria: I’ll push the quota caps via the API gateway:
```
PATCH /admin/kv/ratelimits
{ "scope": "trial,anonymous", "limit": 10, "window_s": 1, "duration_m": 30 }
```

kevin: Turning off embedding-prefetch and reranking for affected endpoints; those were the heavy tail ops.

sophie: Disabling features now: feature-flag:rerank=false, feature-flag:embed-prefetch=false (applied to prod-eu region).

jamal: Early results: P95 down ~300ms within 90s, P99 down ~450ms. Throughput reduced ~18% as expected.

maria: Customer impact: approx 1.8% error spike for long-context requests before mitigation. Top impacted customers by volume: AcmeCorp (chat high-concurrency), Shoply (embeddings pipeline), EduAI (batch evals). I’ve DM’d account reps.

jamal: Good. Create incident ticket with summary + actions + rollback steps. Assign to Maria for postmortem and Kevin for kernel-level followup.

kevin: Noted — we should also update batch kernel selection threshold; current heuristic picks large-kernel when avg_seq_len > 1024 which creates big KV pressure. Propose lowering to 768 as a follow-up.

maria: Handoff — I’m taking on postmortem. Jamal, if you need to step out, @sophie you’re primary for live ops for next 30m.

sophie: Oncall handoff ack. I’ll keep the throttle in place and monitor. If error rates stay <1% and lat stable for 10m, we can gradually relax batch_window to 12ms then 16ms.

incident-bot: Reminder: run automated customer-impact eval: /scripts/impact-check --since 3600000400 --end 3600000800.

maria: Ran quick check: failed requests concentrated on requests > 2000 tokens and rerank-enabled flows. No data leak or SLO breach so far. Logging retention annotated.

jamal: Next steps: 1) keep throttle + feature flags for 30m 2) collect kernel traces for top 3 slow calls 3) schedule rollback plan: restore max_batch_tokens=1024 then batch_window=22ms in staggered steps if P99 < 600ms.

kevin: I’ll capture traces and upload to /incidents/3600000456/traces.tar.gz.

sophie: Monitoring: dashboards updated, alert threshold lowered to +200ms on p99 for next hour.

maria: Notifying sales and support with short template.

jamal: Thanks team. Will follow up in 15m with status. :thumbsup:
